rationale: Extraosseous/extramedullary plasmacytoma is a plasma-cell neoplasm arising in soft tissue outside bone; although ~80% occur in the upper aerodigestive (head/neck) mucosa, authoritative sources document occurrence throughout the body (GI tract, lymph nodes, bladder, breast, thyroid, testis, parotid, skin, CNS), spanning essentially the entire ceiling. The head/neck predilection is a frequency observation, not an anatomic restriction, so the term is not confined to a proper subset.
source_name: NCI SEER Hematopoietic Database (ICD-O-3.2) — Plasmacytoma, extramedullary

term: B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma
rationale: CLL/SLL (and all its synonyms) is a systemic mature B-cell neoplasm involving blood, marrow, lymph nodes, spleen and virtually any nodal/extranodal tissue (skin, GI tract, CNS, liver, lung, etc.); it is not anatomically restricted to a proper subset of its ceiling. These are broad, multi-site lymphoid morphologic entities, so not site-specific.

rationale: Myeloid sarcoma (chloroma / granulocytic sarcoma) is an extramedullary myeloid-blast tumor that can occur at almost any anatomic site of the body except bone marrow (skin, lymph nodes, GI tract, bone, soft tissue, testis, head/neck, brain, lungs, reproductive organs, etc.), spanning the full ceiling. It is therefore not restricted to a proper subset.
